reviews.one_line_contribution: For in-context agent memory, the paper claims the gain a reader keeps from a foreign writer's success-filtered pool is predicted by an offline per-task-type complementarity statistic kappa (the writer's success advantage on the types the reader fails) rather than by writer-reader action agreement, writer strength, item count or trajectory optimality, and it tests this by manipulating writer identity at a fixed per-type item histogram, with a three-arm triple that isolates 'expert solutions to games the reader fails' from 'expert solutions to games the reader already solves' at identical count.
reviews.closest_prior_work: arXiv:2601.14249 (verified via the literature command; ACL, 7 citations, 2026-01-20), 'Which Reasoning Trajectories Teach Students to Reason Better? A Simple Metric of Informative Alignment', proposes Rank-Surprisal Ratio, a metric that explicitly trades alignment (proximity) against informativeness relative to the student's current competence, shows stronger teachers do not necessarily produce better students, and validates the metric for both trajectory selection AND teacher selection. That is the same conceptual claim this proposal calls new: the predictor of transfer is what the teacher supplies that the learner lacks, not the teacher's strength or its similarity to the learner. arXiv:2605.26872 (verified; 'When the Strongest Teacher Is Not the Best Teacher: Student-Centric Answer Selection') makes the strength-is-not-the-predictor half independently. Neither is cited by the proposal, and neither was returned by its collision check. What still separates this proposal: RSR and SCAS are gradient-time distillation with a likelihood/gradient-based statistic and no matched-cost self-collected control, whereas here the reader is frozen and in-context, kappa is a coverage statistic computed from success rates alone before any transfer cell, and the denominator is the reader's own pool at matched episode budget. So this is a domain port with a different (much coarser) statistic, not an independent discovery — an AC will read the headline as 'informative alignment, redone for retrieval-augmented agents'. Among the proposal's own citations, Agent Memory Distillation (2608.07169, verified, 2 citations) is the closest agent-memory work and genuinely does not measure teacher-student compatibility or run a self-pool control; 2210.08073 (verified, CoRL 2022) measures demonstration compatibility for a base policy but not demonstrator-learner complementarity for an in-context reader.
reviews.strongest_objection: The design cannot separate 'foreign' from 'complementary'. Per-type count matching forces every bank onto the reader's own type histogram, so the only surviving difference between a high-kappa foreign bank and the reader's self bank is that the foreign items come from games the reader fails. P3 then confirms that items from failed games carry the gain — but there is no arm in which the READER's own successes on the games it usually fails are supplied at the same count. Since the self pool is success-filtered at ~0.53, such successes are cheaply obtainable (resample the failure-type training games at higher temperature or best-of-n for a few thousand episodes, well inside this budget). Without that arm, the paper's practical payload — when is it worth importing a foreign writer's experience — is unearned: every P2/P3 result is equally consistent with 'coverage of your failure games is what matters, and you can collect it yourself at matched cost', which would make writer identity irrelevant and reduce kappa to a proxy for 'which games are missing from your bank'. Second-order but real: the low-kappa branch of the headline P2 is confounded by the design's own fill rule (a writer with kappa near 0 has fewer than n_R(t) successes on the weighted types, so its bank is topped up with the reader's own items and Delta_m is pushed to 0 mechanically). The entailment check names this and prescribes the fix; the proposal did not adopt it. Third: kappa has six degrees of freedom on ALFWorld, the 0.08/0.02 thresholds are unmotivated, and the proposal's own risk section concedes the class table may be degenerate, in which case the headline rests on two or three cells and the Fisher 2x2 has no power.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Add the self-complement arm: re-collect the reader's own successes on its failure-type training games at a stated matched episode budget and run self_comp against X_comp at identical per-type count. That converts a coverage result into the paper's actual claim about writer identity, and it is the only way any of P2-P4 can support the title. (2) Adopt the entailment check's fix for the low-kappa branch — restrict low-kappa cells to fill = 0, or report Delta_m recomputed on writer-sourced retrievals only — and pre-register a stated action if the Q<->E kappas do not both clear 0.08 rather than leaving the mutual-gain sub-prediction conditional on a measurement not yet taken. (3) Token-match the triple (X_comp trajectories on failed games are longer than X_int trajectories on solved games) or report trajectory length as a pre-registered covariate; blind3 bounds length only at the k=3 wrong-type token count, not the X_comp/X_int length gap. (4) Cite and position against 2601.14249 and 2605.26872, and state explicitly what kappa buys over an RSR-style likelihood statistic — ideally by computing both offline and pre-registering which one classifies the eight cross cells correctly. That would turn the weakest part of the novelty argument into a second competing-predictor test alongside the existing overall-k=0 2x2. (5) Narrow P1a's equivalence band: +/-7 is 0.4 of the Gate-0 effect, so 'proximity is inert' currently passes for any true effect up to about a quarter of the whole phenomenon.
reviews.missing_baseline: The reader's own success-filtered trajectories on the games it usually fails, at the same per-type count as X_comp (obtained by resampling the failure-type training games at higher temperature / best-of-n, with the extra episodes charged to the matched-cost budget). The plan has self_int (reader's own solutions to games it solves) but no self_comp, so writer identity and game-subset complementarity are never crossed at the complementary corner. A reviewer will also ask for the natural (non-count-matched) foreign pools for more than reader Q at more than 2 seeds, since count matching discards 40-50% of expert items and the paper concedes the matched rho understates the natural one.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision on the full claim; the proposal's check is above average for this program but has one blind spot that costs it. Channel for every query below: the literature command (s2cli.py, Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace; both channels reported ok). WebSearch was unavailable in this session and was not used. Queries I ran: (1) recent, 'complementarity between demonstrator and learner predicts transfer of demonstrations' -> only robotics/video-demo work (2608.13049, 2607.20033, 2604.06377, 2603.15432, 2507.06219), nothing on the claim. (2) all-years, 'which teacher demonstrations help a student: coverage of student failures versus policy similarity' -> 2605.26872 (When the Strongest Teacher Is Not the Best Teacher), 2607.28048 (SKILL-KD), 2608.06802, 2606.18216, 2306.09299 — the strength-is-not-the-predictor claim is already standard here. (3) recent, closest named method, 'agent memory distillation teacher trajectories memory for smaller student agents without training' -> 2608.07169 confirmed as the closest agent-memory work (2 citations), plus 2606.29961 DuoMem, 2604.24005, 2609.01272; none manipulates writer identity or uses a matched-cost self pool. (4) recent, 'metric to select which teacher model for a given student informative alignment surprisal teacher selection' -> 2601.14249 (RSR), 2604.11290, 2608.04419. (5) recent, 'in-context demonstrations selected from tasks the model fails outperform demonstrations on tasks it already solves' -> 2605.26350 (When Correct Demonstrations Hurt), 2506.04579, 2505.24143 — none makes the failed-games-vs-solved-games contrast at matched count. (6) all-years, 'predicting negative transfer from source model error profile overlap with target model weaknesses' -> nothing relevant (2505.11771, 2301.12618, 2306.06508). (7) recent, 'retained gain ratio self-collected experience pool versus foreign writer ALFWorld matched cost' -> 2608.04003 PAST-Bench, 2512.02543, 2605.20616; no matched-cost self-pool control found, so the brief's G2/G21 hole appears real. Verification: every arXiv ID the novelty argument leans on resolved — 2608.07169, 2605.30723, 2605.23899, 2604.14004, 2606.19911, 1011.0686, 2210.08073, 2306.09082, 2606.09758, 2501.11425 (all via the literature command). Two verification notes against the proposal: 2604.14004 is 'Memory Transfer Learning: How Memories are Transferred Across Domains in Coding Agents' — cross-DOMAIN, not the 'cross-model memory pools' the Related Work calls it; and 2501.11425 is Agent-R (iterative self-training with MCTS-revised trajectories), which is described more tendentiously than its abstract supports. Judgement on the check itself: it ran four query classes with IDs and channels named, including a genuine home-literature query, which is more than most submissions do. But it searched agent-memory and imitation-learning vocabularies and not the distillation data-selection vocabulary where its own mechanism claim already lives, and so missed 2601.14249 and 2605.26872 — the two papers a reviewer will bring to the discussion. Novelty is scored on what survives that: the in-context/matched-cost port and the P3/P4 triple, not the 'complementarity beats proximity and strength' headline.
